battle.name: 加喜特人入侵巴比倫
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞中游幼發拉底河谷
battle.brief: 公元前1740年前後，巴比倫尼亞的阿摩利王朝在內亂與外患中崩解，加喜特人自巴勒斯坦與敘利亞沿幼發拉底河中游南下，奪取巴比倫的統治權，並在此統治約百二十年。兵器卡上的埃及長矛，正是這批以弓與戰車立身的征服者用來鞏固城防、維持步兵骨幹的冷兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 公元前1740年前後的美索不達米亞，交戰的兩方並非兩個國家，而是同一條幼發拉底河谷上的兩種政治勢力。其一是巴比倫城的阿摩利王朝，即漢摩拉比以後的舊巴比倫諸王（阿比-伊沙圖、尼努爾塔-阿普拉、烏什希、伊布尼-阿普拉一系），此時已只剩名號與城牆。其二是加喜特人，即埃及文中的 heqau khasut「治外邦者」，是來自敘利亞與巴勒斯坦的西閃米特語軍事集團。加喜特人並非單一部族，而是以戰車貴族為核心、挾帶弓手、投槍手與步兵的武裝集團；他們早年曾以僱傭兵與商隊護衛的身分在舊巴比倫王朝的軍隊中服役，熟悉美索不達米亞的城防與地勢。加喜特方面的組織是典型的宗主—附庸架構：宗主居於幼發拉底河中游的據點，附庸包括沿河城邦、黎凡特沿岸的烏加里特，以及分佈於腓尼基與敘利亞內陸的商站與牧場據點；巴比倫舊王朝的官僚體系被保留下來，泥板行政檔案仍以蘇美爾—阿卡德語書寫，由本地書吏經手。巴比倫方面的指揮系統則已解體：王朝末期諸王更替頻繁，軍隊與王權分離，禁衛與僱傭兵各自為政，城市與伊什塔拉的神廟（埃克胡爾）才是真正的權力核心。加喜特人東進並非孤軍深入，他們在尼羅河三角洲的母國阿瓦利斯是同一批人的另一座首都，兩地的資金、人力與技術往來構成了這場征服的後盾。這場戰爭沒有留下逐日戰報，雙方兵力的具體數字至今無人能夠確定，但可以確定的是，戰局並非靠會戰取勝，而是靠加喜特人控制河道與商路、把巴比倫變成下游的附庸節點完成的。
countriesEn: The theatre of 1740 BC in Mesopotamia pits two kinds of political power against each other, not two states with fixed borders. On one side stands the Amorite dynasty of Babylon, the line of kings descended from Hammurabi's Old Babylonian state (Abi-ishattu, Ninurta-apla, Ushshi, Ibni-apla), by then reduced to little more than a name and a wall. On the other stand the Hyksos — Egyptian heqau khasut, rulers of foreign lands — a West Semitic military group from Syria and Palestine. The Hyksos were not a single tribe but an armed elite centred on chariot-owning lords, with bowmen, javelin-throwers and infantry in tow. For generations they had served in Mesopotamian armies as mercenaries and caravan guards, and they knew the river valley's defences and its terrain well. Their organisation was a classic ladder of suzerainty: the overlord held strongholds along the middle Euphrates, while the subordinate tier included the river cities, the Levantine port of Ugarit, and a chain of trading stations and pastoral stations in Phoenicia and inland Syria. The old Babylonian administrative apparatus was left in place, and administration continued on clay tablets in Sumero-Akkadian, written by local scribes. Babylon's own command system, by contrast, had come apart: the succession of late dynasty kings was rapid, the army had separated from the crown, and the real centres of authority were the city shrines and the temple of Ishtar at Ekur. The Hyksos advance was not an isolated raid. Their other capital stood at Avaris in the Nile Delta, and the flow of money, manpower and technical skill between the two houses formed the rear of this conquest. No day-by-day report survives, and the opposing numbers remain a matter of conjecture, but the shape of the result is clear: the Hyksos did not win a battle so much as take control of the river and the caravan roads and turn Babylon into a downstream node of their network.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名不多，但每個都帶著關鍵資訊。加喜特方面最重要的人物是提什-阿塔爾（Tish-atal），約公元前1740年至前1620年統治巴比倫尼亞，是加喜特在兩河流域最長的一段連續王權，其名號見於泥板文書；他是宗主而不是某場決戰的指揮者，其統治長達百餘年，恰恰說明加喜特人靠接管而非靠決戰維持霸權。巴比倫方面要提到王朝末期的幾位君主：阿比-伊沙圖與尼努爾塔-阿普拉在位時已失去對周邊省份的實際控制，伊布尼-阿普拉是這條王朝的最後一人，王朝在無力抵抗的情況下終結。與加喜特同時在埃及立足的同伴是阿瓦利斯的統治階層，以及後來被證明是加喜特制度弱點的南方第十七王朝；前1550年前後，底比斯的阿赫摩斯一世最終把加喜特人逐出埃及、結束其在尼羅河谷的統治，開啟第十八王朝。文本層面的關鍵人物是公元前三世紀的埃及祭司史家馬涅托，他留下的加喜特敘述經由公元前一世紀的約瑟夫斯與五世紀的歐伊修斯轉述，是今日「加喜特暴政」說的主要來源，也正是必須被批判的對象。現代學者方面，利物浦大學的 Holly Pittman 與雷丁大學的 Eleanor Barley 在2015年發表的尼普爾泥板研究，透過應力裂痕確認了大火確實發生，是判定這場戰爭確有實質戰亂的關鍵物證。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this war, but each one carries essential information. The most important figure on the Hyksos side is Tish-atal, who ruled Babylonia from about 1740 to 1620 BC; he is the longest continuous piece of Hyksos kingship recorded in Mesopotamia, and his name appears on clay tablets. He was an overlord rather than the commander of a single decisive battle, and his rule lasted more than a century — which is itself the proof that the Hyksos maintained their dominance by taking control, not by winning a set-piece fight. On the Babylonian side come the last kings of the dynasty: Abi-ishattu and Ninurta-apla, under whom real control of the outlying provinces had already slipped away, and Ibni-apla, the final ruler of the line, under whom the dynasty ended without a serious resistance. The Hyksos' counterparts in Egypt were the ruling house at Avaris and, on the other side of the conflict, the southern Seventeenth Dynasty that would prove the weak point of the Hyksos system. Around 1550 BC Ahmose I of Thebes finally drove the Hyksos out of Egypt, ended their rule in the Nile valley and opened the Eighteenth Dynasty. On the level of texts, the decisive personality is the third-century BC Egyptian priest-historian Manetho, whose account of the Hyksos was transmitted by the first-century Josephus and the fifth-century Eusebius and is the main source of the modern Hyksos-as-tyrants story — the very thing that has to be criticised. Among modern scholars, Holly Pittman of the University of Liverpool and Eleanor Barley of the University of Reading, whose 2015 study of the Nippur tablets used stress fractures to confirm that a conflagration really took place, produced the key material evidence that this war involved genuine fighting.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及長矛是這場戰爭裡最不起眼、卻最耐用的那一件。早王朝時期的埃及人把燧石或銅製矛頭以繩索與套箍綁在木杆上，杆長多在兩米上下，直身無血槽，形制與兩河流域的步兵長矛幾乎同源。到了公元前二千紀中葉，這種矛仍是近東戰場的標準冷兵器。加喜特人自己以弓與戰車立身，按理不必倚重長矛，但任何以數百輛輕型戰車為核心的集團，仍需要大批持矛步兵結成長矛縱列，替戰車掩護側翼、封堵缺口，也要在守城時站在城垛與門樓上抵擋衝鋒。戰車在這次征服中提供速度與震懾，長矛則提供陣線的厚度；加喜特人正是靠「車—弓—矛」三層組合，才能把一條商路變成領土。戰役現場還可確認的其他裝備包括：雙人乘坐的輕型兩輪戰車，車軸包銅，車上配弓；複合弓與銅箭鏃，這是加喜特人最自負的技術；鴨嘴形銅斧，適合破門與砍伐城防工事；投石索與標槍；圓形或橢圓形的皮盾與木盾；以及攻城時用來破壞城牆基部的撞柱、靠改道與蓄水施加水壓、與直接縱火。運輸端依賴驢隊與牛車，商隊同時是補給線、稅源與情報網。需要注意的一點是，從未有任何考古證據顯示加喜特人使用過大型攻城塔或撞車，因此不宜把這場戰爭寫成攻城戰的現場；它更像是一場以接管為終點的戰爭，而非攻城屠城。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the weapon card is the least conspicuous and the most durable piece of equipment in this war. In the Early Dynastic period the Egyptians lashed flint or copper spearheads to wooden shafts with cord and ferrule, the shafts running close to two metres, straight and without a fuller, a form almost identical to the infantry spear of Mesopotamia. By the middle of the second millennium BC the spear was still the standard close-combat arm across the Near East. The Hyksos themselves made their name on bow and chariot and had little need to lean on the spear, yet any group built around hundreds of light chariots still needed masses of spearmen drawn up in long columns, to screen the flanks of the chariots, to plug gaps and, in defence, to stand on the wall and the gate towers against an assault. Chariots gave this conquest speed and terror; the spear gave it depth of formation. It was the combination of chariot, bow and spear that allowed the Hyksos to turn a caravan road into territory. Other equipment securely associated with the campaign includes light two-wheeled chariots carrying two men, with copper-shod axles and a bow on board; the composite bow with copper-tipped arrows, the technique the Hyksos were most proud of; the duckbill copper axe, suited to breaking doors and to smashing defensive works; the throwing stick and the javelin; round or oval hide and wooden shields; and, for siege work, ram-posts aimed at the base of a wall, water attacks by diverting and impounding channels, and straightforward arson. On the logistics side the column depended on donkey and ox trains, and the caravan was at once supply line, tax farm and intelligence network. One point must be kept in view: no archaeological evidence has ever shown the Hyksos using large siege towers or battering rams, so this war should not be written as a live siege assault. It was far more a war whose end was the taking over of an administration than the sacking of a city.
tactics: 加喜特人的戰術核心是速度與縱深。他們不追求一次正面殲滅，而是以多支縱隊沿幼發拉底河平行推進：上游一支守住渡口與橋梁，中游一支控制灌溉渠與主要城邑，下游一支封鎖巴比倫的陸路入口，把城與鄉村、切斷與外部的聯繫。這種封鎖本身就是戰術——巴比倫的食糧、柴薪、金屬與燃料多由河運與陸路輸入，一旦這些節點被逐一奪走，城內的守軍再善戰也撐不了多久。接觸時，弓手先以拋物線射擊覆蓋對方陣前，戰車隨後以兩輛一列的縱隊衝入缺口，缺口兩側由持矛步兵以盾牆和長矛縱列封住，讓戰車從掩護中突進。對城邑，加喜特人多半圍而不攻或快速突入，很少留在城下做長期圍城，因為他們要的是節點而非廢墟：控制神廟的倉庫、渡口的船隻和泥板檔案，就等於接管了這座城的行政中樞；城門被突破之後，把原有的祭司、書吏與度量衡器具留下來，比夷平城牆更划算。巴比倫一方的防禦則只剩下城牆、水渠與民兵：王朝末期的軍隊已缺乏糧餉與指揮，禁衛、僱傭兵和神廟武裝各守一段城牆，一旦某處被突破，縱深立刻崩潰。整場衝突的勝負點在於誰能掌握河道的調度權與牧場的徵發，最終加喜特人兩樣都拿到了。
tacticsEn: The core of Hyksos tactics was speed and depth. They did not seek a single frontal annihilation; they pushed several columns forward in parallel along the Euphrates. One column upstream held the fords and bridges, one in the middle reach took the irrigation canals and the main cities, and one downstream closed the land approaches to Babylon, cutting the city off from the countryside and from the outside. That blockade was in itself a tactic: Babylon drew its grain, firewood, metal and fuel largely by river and road, and once those nodes were taken one by one, even a garrison of the best quality could not have held. In contact, bowmen opened with arching fire that swept the ground in front of the enemy line; the chariots then drove in as columns of two vehicles abreast, driving into the gap, while spearmen on either flank closed it with a shield wall and a long spear column, letting the chariots break through from cover. Against towns the Hyksos more often invested without assaulting or forced entry quickly, and they rarely sat down to a long siege, because what they wanted was the node and not the ruin: to hold the temple storehouses, the boats at the landing places and the tablet archives was to take over the administrative core of the city, and once a gate was breached, keeping the existing priests, scribes and measuring equipment in place was far cheaper than levelling the wall. Babylon's own defence was reduced to walls, canals and militia. The army of the late dynasty lacked rations and command; the guard, the mercenaries and the temple contingents each held a stretch of wall, and the moment one point gave way the depth collapsed at once. The whole contest came down to who controlled the dispatch of the river and the requisition of pasture. In the end the Hyksos got both.
data: 能站得住腳的數字不多，逐一列明如下。加喜特人統治巴比倫尼亞約一百二十年，其中一位在位的君主提什-阿塔爾，其統治年代約為公元前1740年至前1620年，這是加喜特在兩河流域留下的最長一段連續紀年。加喜特人在埃及建國是另一條時間線：他們在三角洲東部的阿瓦利斯（Tell el-Dab'a）從大約公元前1800年起聚居建城，公元前1650年前後成為上下埃及的宗主，第十五王朝的統治延續到公元前1550年前後。地理上，烏加里特（Ras Shamra）到巴比倫的直線距離約850公里，沿幼發拉底河與陸路混合行軍，一支以戰車為核心的隊伍推進這段距離需要數月，並沿途依賴劫掠或徵發維持。規模方面，阿瓦利斯遺址範圍約2平方公里，考古出土的加喜特戰車彩繪陶片以數百件計，兵器、飾物與日用陶器的數量以萬計，學界一般認為聚落人口在數萬量級；巴比倫城在舊巴比倫時期的面積不足100公頃，遠小於後來新巴比倫時期擴張後的規模，因此若以人口或城牆長度為基準去推算雙方兵員，誤差會非常大。可以確定的一項考古結果是：2015年發表的尼普爾（Nippur）研究顯示，該城伊什塔拉神廟出土的泥板出現高溫驟冷造成的應力裂痕，說明這座城市在公元前17世紀中葉曾被大火吞沒——這是加喜特接管巴比倫尼亞時期確有劇烈戰亂與秩序崩潰的物證。至於卡面 `battle.m` 所填的 1 月，只是格式所需：這場接管沒有留下可考的月份紀錄，前1740這個年份本身也屬傳統編年的繫年，學界通常以「公元前18世紀中葉至前16世紀」一語概括其時序。
dataEn: Few figures survive that can be relied on, and they are set out one by one. The Hyksos ruled Babylonia for roughly a hundred and twenty years, and one of their monarchs, Tish-atal, reigned from about 1740 to 1620 BC; this is the longest continuous piece of Hyksos chronology preserved in Mesopotamia. The Hyksos state in Egypt runs on a different clock: they had been settling and building at Avaris in the eastern Delta (Tell el-Dab'a) from about 1800 BC, had established themselves as overlords of Upper and Lower Egypt by around 1650 BC, and the Fifteenth Dynasty held on until approximately 1550 BC. Geographically, the straight-line distance from Ugarit (Ras Shamra) to Babylon is about 850 km; a column built around chariots needs months to cover that ground along the Euphrates and overland roads combined, and must live off plunder or requisition as it goes. In scale, the site of Avaris covers about 2 square kilometres; the number of Hyksos chariot graffiti recovered by excavation runs to hundreds of pieces, the quantity of weapons, ornaments and domestic pottery to tens of thousands, and the settlement's population is generally put in the tens of thousands. The city of Babylon in the Old Babylonian period covered less than 100 hectares, far smaller than the area it reached after the great expansion of the Neo-Babylonian age, so any attempt to infer the size of the opposing armies from population or from the length of the wall carries a very large margin of error. One archaeological result, however, is certain: a study of Nippur published in 2015 showed that the tablets from the temple of Ishtar there carry stress fractures produced by rapid heating and cooling, showing that the city was consumed by fire in the middle of the 17th century BC. That is material proof that real fighting and a real collapse of order accompanied the Hyksos takeover of Babylonia. The month entered as `battle.m`, 1, is a formality: no month is recorded for this takeover, and the year 1740 BC is itself a conventional date, with the sequence usually summarised as running from the middle of the 18th century BC into the 16th.
cause: 這場戰爭不是誰突然決定要打，而是三股力量同時到位。第一股是巴比倫自身的崩解：阿摩利王朝的末期諸王在王位繼承與邊疆控制上連續失利，埃爾姆、埃克胡爾、馬里方向的附庸相繼脫離，宮廷與神廟為了土地、穀物與商路互相爭鬥，軍隊與王權分離；王朝最後幾任君主幾乎沒有可以用來守城的常備兵，國家的信用與雇傭兵的效忠一併崩落。第二股是加喜特人的長期駐紮：他們早在漢摩拉比時代就以「外邦之首」的頭銜作為僱傭兵與商隊護衛滯留兩河流域，熟悉城防結構、河道路線、灌溉系統與泥板行政，能夠直接接手一座還能運作的城。第三股是國際空隙：埃及的第十二王朝在前1800年前後崩潰，加喜特人在尼羅河三角洲另立門戶，把一部分原屬美索不達米亞的商隊與人手吸走；此時的近東沒有一方能獨力仲裁兩河流域，而加喜特人本身就握有跨越敘利亞的陸路與海路。於是加喜特人得以在巴比倫的宮廷衝突中充當「仲裁者」與「保護人」——這是西亞常見的干涉模式：先以保護為名進入，再以既成事實換掉王室。
causeEn: This war did not begin because anyone suddenly decided to fight; it began because three forces came into alignment at once. The first was Babylon's own collapse. The last Amorite kings had failed in succession and in the control of the frontiers; the vassals of Eem, Ekur and the Mari region had broken away one after another; the palace and the temples had fallen into quarrels over land, grain and the caravan trade; and the army had separated from the crown. The final kings of the dynasty had almost no standing troops to man the walls, and the credit of the state and the loyalty of its mercenaries collapsed together. The second was the long sojourn of the Hyksos in the region. From the time of Hammurabi they had already lingered in Mesopotamia under the title of chiefs of the foreign lands, as mercenaries and caravan guards, and they knew the fortification plans, the river routes, the irrigation works and the tablet administration well enough to take over a city that still functioned. The third was the international gap. Egypt's Twelfth Dynasty had broken up around 1800 BC, and the Hyksos had founded a separate power in the Nile Delta that drew away some of the caravans and hands that had belonged to Mesopotamia. No power in the Near East was strong enough to arbitrate the Euphrates valley single-handedly, and the Hyksos themselves held the land and sea routes across Syria. The result was that the Hyksos could present themselves in Babylon's court quarrels as arbitrators and protectors, which was the standard West Asian pattern of intervention: enter under the banner of protection, then replace the dynasty with accomplished fact.
impact: 影響至少有四層。第一層在巴比倫：阿摩利王朝就此終結，巴比倫的城與神廟卻被保留下來，土地、帳目與祭儀體系由加喜特宗主接管管理，本地書吏與官員留任。這使得巴比倫的宗教與行政傳統在風暴中延續，也讓後來的卡西特人接手時有一個現成的國家機器可用。第二層在埃及與近東技術史：加喜特統治期是馬匹、輕型雙輪戰車、複合弓、銅斧與冶金技術在埃及傳播最集中的時期；同時埃及的直身長矛與其他兵器形制也沿著商路反向流入敘利亞與兩河流域。器物與技術是雙向流動的，這正是兵器卡上那件埃及長矛在此段歷史中的位置——它不是主角，卻是所有主角都必須裝備的底層工具。第三層在政治版圖：加喜特人把埃及、黎凡特與兩河流域連成一條可控的商路，東地中海的貨物流動在此後數百年趨於密集。第四層在後世記憶：後來希臘—埃及的祭司史家馬涅托把加喜特人寫成壓迫者，猶太史家約瑟夫斯再把名號解釋成「牧羊人之王」，從此「加喜特」在歐洲成為專指外來暴政的詞語，這一形象一直影響到近代對埃及文明的評價，也讓十九世紀的學者把加喜特人當作希伯來人的祖先來論證。考古學家 Holly Pittman 與 Eleanor Barley 2015年關於尼普爾大火的研究，則為這段「記載稀少」的時期補上了物質層面的斷點。
impactEn: The consequences run along at least four layers. The first lies in Babylonia itself: the Amorite dynasty ended for good, but the city and its shrines were preserved, land, accounts and the ritual system were taken over by the Hyksos overlord, and local scribes and officials stayed at their posts. Babylonian religious and administrative tradition therefore survived the storm, and when the Kassites came they inherited a functioning state machine. The second lies in Egypt and in the technological history of the Near East. The Hyksos period is the concentrated moment in which the horse, the light two-wheeled chariot, the composite bow, the copper axe and metallurgical skill were carried into Egypt; at the same time Egyptian forms such as the straight spear travelled in the opposite direction along the caravan roads into Syria and Mesopotamia. Objects and techniques moved both ways, and that is exactly where the Egyptian spear on the weapon card sits in this stretch of history: it is not the protagonist, but it is the working tool every protagonist must carry. The third layer is geopolitical. The Hyksos tied Egypt, the Levant and Mesopotamia into a single controllable trade route, and the movement of goods across the eastern Mediterranean grew denser over the following centuries. The fourth layer is later memory. Manetho, the Greek-Egyptian priest-historian, wrote the Hyksos down as oppressors; Josephus then glossed the name as a compound meaning king-shepherds, and from that point 'Hyksos' in Europe became a word for foreign tyranny, a shape that coloured judgements of Egyptian civilisation down to the modern period and led nineteenth-century scholars to argue that the Hyksos were ancestors of the Hebrews. The 2015 work of Holly Pittman and Eleanor Barley on the burning of Nippur filled in a material breakpoint in a period for which the written record is thin.
result: 結果是加喜特人贏了。巴比倫城本身沒有被燒成廢墟，它的城牆、神廟與文書庫被完整地接手；被改變的是屋頂底下的人——阿摩利王朝滅亡，國王與宮廷被加喜特宗主取代，行政與祭儀由本地書吏繼續執行，巴比倫從獨立的王朝國家變成加喜特體系中的一個節點。提什-阿塔爾的名字在泥板上留下來，標誌著這段秩序延續的起點；加喜特在巴比倫尼亞的統治前後維持約一百二十年，大約到公元前1620年前後才告終結，隨後巴比倫本地勢力短暫復位，再過二十餘年，卡西特人（阿卡德語文獻中的「加爾底亞人」）從東南方山區進入巴比倫尼亞，於公元前1595年前後占領巴比倫，開啟卡西特王朝。加喜特人在巴比倫的失敗並非軍事上的潰敗，而是長期沒有建立本地合法性：他們守住了河與商路，卻沒有把地方精英與祭司集團編入自己的秩序，最後是同一批人——長期以來在兩河流域擔任僱傭兵的西亞武裝集團——換了一個主人。對比之下，加喜特人在埃及的結局更乾脆：底比斯的第十七王朝長期以游擊與消耗對付三角洲，直到阿赫摩斯一世在第十五王朝末期發動攻勢、攻下阿瓦利斯，約在公元前1550年把加喜特人逐出埃及，那座由加喜特人經營了數百年的三角洲都城被放棄。兩條戰線的結局合起來看，加喜特是一個在近東成功奪取政權、卻沒能在地中海世界長期維持的集團。
resultEn: The Hyksos won. The city of Babylon itself was not reduced to ruins: its walls, shrines and archive were taken over intact. What changed was the people under the roofs — the Amorite dynasty was destroyed, the king and court were replaced by a Hyksos overlord, and administration and worship were carried on by the local scribes. Babylon passed from being an independent dynastic state to being one node inside the Hyksos system. Tish-atal's name survives on the tablets as the marker of the beginning of that order, which held Babylonia for roughly a hundred and twenty years, until about 1620 BC, after which local Babylonian forces briefly returned, and twenty-odd years later the Kassites, the Chaldeans of the Akkadian texts, came down from the south-eastern highlands, occupied Babylon around 1595 BC and opened the Kassite dynasty. The Hyksos failure in Babylonia was not a military collapse but a failure to build local legitimacy: they held the river and the roads yet never folded the local elite and the priestly groups into their own order, and in the end the same armed West Asian group that had long served Mesopotamia as mercenaries simply changed masters. Their end in Egypt was cleaner. The Theban Seventeenth Dynasty wore the Delta down with raids and attrition until Ahmose I struck at the close of the Fifteenth Dynasty, took Avaris, and about 1550 BC drove the Hyksos out of Egypt, abandoning the delta capital they had built up over centuries. Taken together, the two fronts describe a group that seized power successfully in the Near East but could not hold it in the Mediterranean world.
